text:
Jana: Heads-up: long-run soak on dedicated-a100 shows steady KV residency growth for our long-context traces (~50k tokens). Resident kvcache keeps climbing ~1.1GB/hr, no plateau.

Mike: Same runtime SHA across pools? any config diffs between hosted/dedicated/private?

Jana: runtime v2.14.2 everywhere. Diff summary: dedicated nodes have hugepages enabled, jemalloc arena tweaks, and we set kv_page_align=64k for NUMA. Hosted uses 4k alignment and default jemalloc. Private onprem varies (some have hugepages forced).

Alex R: can you paste a quick memory map or a small pmap snippet?

Jana: pmap excerpt:
```
pid 24411
15.2G total
kvcache: 10.1G rw-p
kv-frames: 4.0G rw-p
other: 1.1G
```
Resident kvcache increases monotonically, not spikes.

Lee: any extra pagefaults or swap churn reported? dmesg noise?

Jana: pagefault counters normal, swap 0. dmesg shows rare TLB flush notes for NVLink but nothing screaming OOM.

Mike: hypothesis: hugepages + 64k alignment magnify allocator fragmentation so frames canno longer be coalesced or released back to OS. Also batching semantics may keep refcounts slightly above zero for many frames.

Alex R: replayed traces: longctx traffic sends lots of interleaved small requests that touch a broad set of slot chains. Because the batching window is long, we keep per-request holders alive and eviction can't free them.

Jana: eviction logs (sample):
```
evict_attempts: 950/sec
evict_reclaimed: 30/sec
slot_ref_zero_events: very low
```

Mike: that low reclaim rate suggests frames are still referenced. Could be a regression in the request-holder release path under v2.14.x when continuous batching hits.

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T09:12:19 by shipbot 9 rolled runtime v2.14.2 to dedicated-a100 pool

Alex R: quick experiment proposal: run a canary that sets kv_page_align=4k on a subset and reduce batching max window from 250ms->80ms. Also try jemalloc coalesce options.

Jana: spun up 4 canary nodes with both toggles ~30min ago. Early telemetry: kvcache resident down ~250MB and growth slope flattened.

Lee: Private/onprem differences matter: some boxes pinned hugepages at boot and run kernel 5.10; MTU differences (9k vs 1500) change RPC batching behavior which can indirectly affect reuse. I'll gather kernel param matrix.

Mike: note: kernel-selected memcpy/attention kernels differ across hosts. A fallback memcopy kernel we saw on dedicated creates additional scratch allocations which sit in process heap alongside KV and worsen residency. Need to compare kernel_select logs.

Jana: kernel_select excerpt from canary dedicated: 
```
kernel_select: cpu_opt -> memcopy_fallback_v3 during regen windows
kv_alloc_samples: steady 1100/sec
evict_calls: 820/sec, reclaimed: 45/sec
```
(evict reclaim improved slightly on canary)

Alex R: action items proposal:
1) Keep canary running 24h with kv_page_align=4k + batching_window=80ms.
2) Add temporary metrics to emit slot-holder refcounts and per-frame holder stack to find why refcount != 0.
3) Try jemalloc background coalesce on canary (toggleable).
4) Run identical longctx synthetic workload on hosted and private to compare kernel selections and memory layout.

Jana: doing (1) and (3) now. (2) needs a small test build; ETA ~3-4h.

Lee: opened infra ticket to collect kernel versions, hugepage status, NUMA and MTU across pools. infra-ticket #3245 assigned to me.

Mike: if canary holds, mitigation plan: reduce batching window in dedicated config and enable jemalloc coalescing globally for dedicated pool, then monitor. Longer term: strengthen eviction heuristic to consider pinned-window and reuse frequency (LRU+pin-aware), not only age.

Alex R: also add a deterministic toggle for kernel selection to avoid picking a kernel path that allocates ephemeral scratch pages on enterprise/private boxes. We should be able to favor the memory-friendly kernel on those deployments.

Jana: canary @ 2h: slope stable vs previous run. Will post 24h results.

Mike: add a pre-release smoke test for memory-residency growth on long-context traces so future patches don't regress refcount release. :memo:

Alex R: agree. add nightly e2e with longctx synthetic workload into CI to catch slow leaks.

Jana: thanks all, I9ll update here when 24h is done. :thumbsup:
